title: K-pop��s $301M Export Boom Hides a Cooling Home Market
excerpt: K-pop album exports reached $301.74M in 2025, but domestic physical sales fell for a second straight year. Here is why that gap matters in 2026.
content:
Start with the contradiction: K-pop album exports broke the $300 million mark in 2025, yet domestic physical sales declined for a second consecutive year. The same industry is expanding globally while losing momentum at home. The real question is no longer whether K-pop is growing, but what kind of growth model is now taking over.

## Exports hit a record high, but local sentiment says something else
### The export side is clear
Reports from KBS World and Korea JoongAng Daily show K-pop album exports reached about $301.74 million in 2025, up 3.4% year on year. Japan, China, and the United States remained the top import markets. In other words, the global fan-purchase engine is still intact.

### Domestic consumption tells a different story
At the same time, the local market narrative has shifted. Instead of broad mainstream hits, agencies are increasingly optimized for high-value core fandoms. Revenue can stay resilient while cultural penetration weakens ? that asymmetry is now visible.

## A majority-overseas revenue structure is becoming standard
### How major labels are now mixed
A February 2026 Korea JoongAng Daily analysis reported that, from January to September 2025, overseas sales represented a majority share for most major agencies (HYBE 59%, JYP 60%, YG 51%, SM 35%). This is a structural signal: growth is now tied less to domestic chart dominance and more to global touring and fandom monetization.

![Infographic comparing rising K-pop exports and softening domestic demand](/images/news/kpop-domestic-global-gap-1.png)
_A dual-track K-pop market: global expansion alongside domestic cooling._

### Why investors are reading it this way
A Korea Times report linked 2026 earnings expectations to potential full-group activity by BTS and BIGBANG. That framing matters: market valuation is increasingly driven by global event catalysts rather than domestic mainstream traction.

## Why the Korean market still matters
### Domestic performance remains a credibility layer
Even in a global-first cycle, local success still acts as a certification mark. For smaller agencies in particular, domestic chart and broadcast visibility remains an onboarding channel for global discovery.

### What to watch over the next 12 months
Track both lines together: (1) global indicators such as exports and tour attendance, and (2) local indicators such as streaming penetration and crossover hits. If only one side performs, short-term numbers may hold ? but long-term brand durability can weaken.

## MEARROW��s view on the split market
KCL sees 2026 as a "growth-with-separation" phase. Global upside should continue, but if emotional relevance in Korea keeps shrinking, IP lifespan could shorten. The likely winners will be teams that monetize globally while continuously rebuilding local narrative power.

## The next benchmark starts now
The core competition in K-pop is no longer just about views. It is about sustaining both global revenue and domestic cultural gravity at the same time. Crossing $300 million is a milestone ? but the real test is who can preserve that balance for the next three years.
